title: Who will win the 2026 Ballon d'Or?
resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the winner of the men's 2026 Ballon d'Or, expected to be awarded on October 26, 2026.
fine_print: If the winner is not one of the listed options, the question will resolve as Other. If the Ballon d'Or is not awarded for any reason before January 1, 2027, this question will be annulled.
background:
Every year, the [Ballon d'Or](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballon_d'Or) is awarded to the world's best professional footballer (soccer player), as judged by [*France Football*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France_Football). Although the criteria have changed over the decades that the award has been given out, the current iteration of the Ballon d'Or is awarded to the player, of any professional league in the world, who gave the best performance over the previous football season.

Lionel Messi has won the Ballon d'Or a record eight times, including most recently in 2023. In 2024, it was won by Rodrigo Hernández Cascante (known simply as Rodri), and in 2025 it was won by Ousmane Dembélé.

On September 8, 2026, the thirty nominees for the 2026 Ballon d'Or were [announced](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/live-blogs/ballon-dor-2026-live-updates-shortlist-nominees/UtaqXQpPuqLX/WdM249iYCFvt/?source=emp_shared_liveblog\&smid=url-share-ta). The nominees include, among many others: Dembélé, of Paris Saint-Germain; Harry Kane, of Bayern Munich; Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, also of Paris Saint-Germain; Kylian Mbappé, of Real Madrid; Messi, of Inter Miami; Rodri, of Barcelona; and Lamine Yamal, also of Barcelona.

Notably, Rodri and Yamal also play for the Spanish national team, which won the 2026 FIFA World Cup, at which Rodri was awarded the [Golden Ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup_awards#Golden_Ball) (not to be confused with the Ballon d'Or) for best player in the tournament. (Messi and Mbappé were the runners-up.)

comments.author: Vlad25
comments.text:
**My forecast: Yamal 50%, Kane 43%, Others 7%**

I've placed Yamal slightly ahead of Kane, mainly because of his World Cup victory with Spain and his season with Barcelona. Historically, and major international trophies such as the world cup have carried significant weight in Ballon d'Or voting.

However, Kane remains a serious contender given his exceptional goalscoring record and domestic success with Bayern Munich. I think his individual performances make this a much closer contest than Yamal's trophy haul might suggest.

I've allocated just 7% across the remaining candidates because the available evidence and betting markets suggest the competition is largely between just these two.

Ultimately, I favour Yamal slightly, but I wouldn't be surprised if Kane won.

comments.author: VectorWright
comments.text:
Going with Kane a bit above Yamal here, roughly 52/43/5.



Market's basically flipped on this one, Kane was behind in late Sept and now he's favorite at something like 55-56%. There's also that "leaked results" thing going around saying Yamal wins and Kane's third, but it's not coming from MARCA (the only outlet that's actually nailed this before), and most of these leaks turn out fake anyway, misspelled names, wrong club, the usual tells. Not putting much weight on it.



Only reason I'm not just taking the market number straight is the World Cup effect. Voters tend to reward winning the World Cup pretty hard in World Cup years and Yamal's got that this time. Kane's stats are nuts (73 goals in 65 games, Bundesliga, Golden Shoe) but stats alone haven't always been enough to beat a World Cup win historically.



So 52/43/5 feels about right. Not a strong edge, mostly just discounting that leak.

comments.author: sai_39
comments.text:
I think this is now essentially a two player race. Yamal has the cleanest combination of individual excellence and major trophies. Barcelona won La Liga and Yamal was officially named [La Liga Player of the Season](https://www.laliga.com/en-ES/news/lamine-yamal-ea-sports-laliga-player-of-the-season-2025-2026), with 16 goals and 12 assists in league play. He then became a World Cup champion with Spain. Kane probably has the strongest pure individual-performance case. He scored 61 goals for Bayern in 2025/26, helping them win both the Bundesliga and DFB-Pokal and reach the Champions League semifinal. He then scored six World Cup goals as England finished third. So the top-two disagreement is effectively:

**Kane:** unprecedented-ish scoring output, domestic double, excellent World Cup.

**Yamal:** somewhat weaker raw numbers, but La Liga Player of the Season and a World Cup winner.

The biggest clue I could find is that the voting reportedly closed on 28 September. That means the result is effectively already fixed. Yamal's subsequent performances cannot alter a single ballot. Yet Yamal has gone from roughly 45% → 58% on Polymarket after voting closed, while Kane has fallen from roughly 42% → 35%. This could be due to market movement, credible journalist ballot disclosures, insider information, or leaks? Traditional bookmakers have now moved in essentially the same direction. An [odds comparison](https://bookies.com/uk/news/ballon-dor-betting-odds-2026-yamal-slight-favourite-over-kane-2-october) published today gives Yamal 7/10, Kane 6/4, Mbappé 22/1, Messi 25/1, Rodri 33/1, Kvaratskhelia 80/1, and Dembélé 175/1. Those correspond to raw implied probabilities of about 59%, 40%, 4.3%, 3.8%, 2.9%, 1.2%, and 0.6% respectively. 

Looking at modern World Cup-linked Ballon d'Or cycles gives a useful pattern:

| Cycle | Ballon d'Or       | World Cup Result                 |
| ----- | ----------------- | -------------------------------- |
| 1998  | Zidane            | World champion                   |
| 2002  | Ronaldo           | World champion                   |
| 2006  | Cannavaro         | World champion                   |
| 2010  | Messi             | Argentina QF                     |
| 2014  | Cristiano Ronaldo | Portugal group stage             |
| 2018  | Modrić            | World Cup finalist + Golden Ball |
| 2023  | Messi             | World champion + Golden Ball     |

So 4 of those 7 winners were World Cup champions, and 5 of 7 reached the World Cup final. The two conspicuous exceptions were Messi in 2010 and Ronaldo in 2014.
